No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=179) meeting sample-size thresholds (I4,I5), and reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates for bvFTD vs controls and interaction effects (I6,I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text and supplementary materials (I8). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, non-empirical, only DTI/FC/cortical thickness, or samples with disallowed comorbidities) apply. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the review focused on bvFTD imaging studies.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=22), meeting sample size requirements. The study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with voxelwise GLM, TFCE, and reports anatomical clusters with MNI coordinates for bvFTD versus controls and covariate analyses (i.e., between-group contrasts in a defined stereotaxic space). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are presented and described in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no excluded comorbidities reported, and not limited to disallowed modalities). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and coordinate tables referenced. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly examines clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) is explicitly used. Sample: 22 bvFTD patients and 35 healthy controls (both >6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses with results localized in MNI space and presents between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and vs AD) with coordinate-based results and figures; covariate VBM analyses and overlap maps are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, or disallowed imaging modality) are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not meet sample-size and group-level whole-brain result requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET was used) and I4 (a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup is present). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (bvFTD patient group n=4, below the required ≥6), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space comparing a bvFTD group to controls — analyses were single-subject SPM comparisons), and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded for not satisfying all required inclusion criteria.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-wise VBM analyses (using MNI standard space) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to controls, with figures and statistical contrasts; sample sizes exceed the minimum (clinical bvFTD n=15; controls n=18). The study therefore meets imaging modality (VBM), sample (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), sample size (≥6), between-group contrasts reported in a defined stereotactic space, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (figures/tables/supplementary). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed modalities-only) are met. Hence include.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19), uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI (I3), meets sample size requirements (I5), and explicitly reports voxelwise, whole-brain group comparisons (VBM contrast bvFTD vs controls and resting-state connectivity differences) with MNI coordinates (I6, I7). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete) and reports results in acceptable formats (figures and coordinates) (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and no evidence of excluded comorbid samples). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This FDG‑PET study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and healthy controls and reports voxelwise SPM analyses; however it does not report a whole‑brain, between‑group voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to controls in stereotactic coordinates. The imaging results are voxelwise correlations between hypometabolism and theory-of-mind deficit scores across the pooled sample (adjusting for pathology), and group comparisons reported are extracted regional CMRglc values (post-hoc ROI/statistical tests) rather than a bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise map with coordinates. Therefore I3, I4 and I5 are satisfied, but I6 and I7 are not met (no between-group voxelwise contrast for bvFTD vs controls clearly reported). Full text appears complete. Excluded because it does not provide the required group-level, whole‑brain between‑group voxelwise results for bvFTD vs controls as specified by the inclusion criteria.

Exclusion (E6) applies: the study used a region-of-interest VBM approach restricted to cortical midline structures rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD N=22 and controls N=17, both ≥6), I6 (reported between-group voxelwise contrasts with coordinates in MNI space for bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (paper does not provide at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample; analyses were ROI-restricted to CMS). Therefore the study must be excluded because it reports only ROI-based VBM results with no whole-brain voxelwise findings, violating the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and whole-brain diffusion tensor imaging (TBSS) to assess grey- and white-matter correlates of disinhibition in clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The sample includes 14 bvFTD patients and 18 controls (and 15 AD patients). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain VBM analyses aligned to MNI space, with between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs AD) and tables/figures of results. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported and described in the text and tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and uses FDG-PET (meets I3, I4, I5), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses or between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Neuroimaging assessment was visual/rating-based and diagnostic (sensitivity/specificity) rather than voxelwise statistical mapping with coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (and by extension I8) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply directly. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the study reports only ROI/parcellation-based network analyses (AAL 116 parcellation and MST on ROI time series) and does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain contrasts in MNI or Talairach space. Exclusion IDs met: E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (patient n=41, control n=39). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates; results are ROI-/node-level), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result). Full text appears complete for assessment (methods, results, figures described). Therefore the paper does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise reporting and must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) nor use an eligible imaging modality. Specifically: (a) Imaging modality: dual-phase 18F-florbetapir PET (amyloid tracer with early perfusion-like frames) is not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — fails I3. (b) Sample: participants are patients with primary progressive aphasia variants (semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia) and Alzheimer’s disease; no clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease participants — fails I4. Although the study has adequate sample sizes (6 PPA patients and 8 controls) satisfying I5, it does not provide between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results relevant to a bvFTD versus control comparison (SPM results are reported for PPA vs controls, not bvFTD) — fails I6 and I7. Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (it uses Freesurfer surface-based ROI volumetric analyses), and it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD sample included) and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=48, controls n=94). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modalities), I6 (no coordinate-based between-group contrasts reported), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI-based analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients included, n=32) and I5 (patient and control groups >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is Freesurfer-derived regional volumetry from T1 MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in stereotactic space/MNI or Talairach comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported), and I8 (no stereotactic coordinates/tables/figures of whole-brain voxelwise results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports regional/ROI analyses using Freesurfer parcellation with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper does not satisfy required imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses both voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET (I3). The FTD sample was clinically diagnosed using consensus criteria and explicitly excluded semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia, indicating the remaining patients represent behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD)/classic FTD (I4). Sample sizes satisfy the minimum (13 FTD patients; 20 controls) (I5). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise SPM comparisons normalized to standard space (MNI), and report between-group contrasts comparing the FTD group to controls and to AD, with tables/figures of results (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbidities reported). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sufficient sample sizes (9 bvFTD patients; controls n=18) meeting I5. It reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise WM results (TBSS/Randomise) comparing bvFTD to controls, consistent with I6 and I7. However, it does NOT use any of the required imaging modalities listed in I3 (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). The imaging modalities are DTI (TBSS and tractography), structural ROI volumetry, and arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion — none of which satisfy I3. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are triggered by the study information provided. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I3 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study includes FDG-PET (I3 met), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4 met), and sufficient sample sizes (I5 met: ~10 patients and 10 controls). However, it does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrast specifically for a bvFTD-only group vs. controls. Group-level analyses are reported as ROI comparisons and ROI-based statistics; voxelwise maps are provided only at the single-subject level (individual patient vs controls), and the patient group is pooled across FTD variants rather than reporting bvFTD-only voxelwise group results. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. This violates the review requirement for group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample. Exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain group results relevant to the review objective) applies. Full text appears complete. Detailed justification: inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I5; inclusion IDs not met: I6, I7; exclusion IDs met: E6.

This study used VBM and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=20) and reports voxelwise coordinates, but its analyses were restricted to a frontal mask and correlate SEA subscores within the bvFTD group rather than reporting any between-group contrast versus healthy controls. Therefore it does not provide a between-group MNI/Talairach contrast of bvFTD vs controls (I6 not met) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results (analyses were region-restricted to a frontal mask) (I7 not met). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the paper reports region-restricted voxelwise/ROI-style analyses with no whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical VBM study in a clinical bvFTD sample meeting all inclusion criteria: VBM was used (I3); participants included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and age/education-matched controls (n=19) meeting sample size requirements (I4,I5); whole-brain voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts and correlational analyses are reported with MNI coordinates (I6,I7); results are presented in main text/tables and ROI/whole-brain analyses are described (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not resting-state seed-FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only, and no indication of disqualifying comorbidities). The provided full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This paper is a study design/protocol of an ongoing observational cohort (LOF study). It describes planned use of MRI, FDG-PET, and CSF and recruitment of patients with late-onset frontal behavioral change (n=130 so far), but it does not present empirical imaging results. It does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor does it present whole-brain coordinate results. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria (I4, I6, I7) and meets exclusion criterion E8 (non-empirical paper/protocol without original imaging results).

Excluded because the study uses cortical thickness (volumetric MRI/cortical thickness) as the morphometric measure and reports cortical thickness results only. This meets exclusion criterion E9 (studies that only report cortical thickness methods are excluded). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present), I5 (patient group n=17 and control group n=22, both >=6), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of cortical thickness in bvFTD vs controls), and I8 (whole-brain results are presented/described in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modalities are VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — cortical thickness is excluded), and I6 (no explicit coordinates in provided full text confirming between-group results reported in MNI/Talairach space). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD sample (n=27) and age-matched healthy controls (n=14). The imaging modality is voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). The sample contains a bv-FTD group meeting the target diagnosis (I4) with more than 6 participants, and the control group also exceeds 6 participants (I5). The authors performed whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses (described in MNI space) and explicitly report group-level VBM comparisons entering each diagnostic group separately versus controls and reference supplementary tables with regions of significant difference; thus there is reporting of between-group whole-brain contrasts involving the bv-FTD group (I6, I7). The paper reports whole-brain results described in main text and references supplementary coordinate tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain VBM, no evidence of disallowed modalities or comorbid psychiatric pooling). Full text appears complete for the main article (supplementary tables noted but their absence is acceptable).

This empirical study meets the review objective and satisfies all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4); the neuroimaging sample meets minimum sizes (8 bvFTD patients in imaging analyses, 16 controls; I5); reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts normalized to MNI space (I6) with tables/figures and voxelwise cluster-corrected results (I7); and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and uses VBM, resting-state fMRI, and 18F-FDG PET (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, it does not include a healthy/control group comparison and does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (in MNI/Talairach space) comparing the bvFTD group to controls; instead, analyses extract ROI-based voxelwise measures from NDH-derived network cores and apply SVM classification across patient groups. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (group-level, whole-brain between-group voxelwise results for bvFTD vs controls) are not met. Exclusion criterion E6 applies (reports only ROI-based/no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion met: E6 (study reports regional/clinical PET ratings and correlations rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise analyses or coordinate tables). Inclusions met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (bvFTD n=13, AD n=18; groups >=6). Inclusions not met: I6 and I7 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables provided). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks whole-brain, voxelwise reporting required by the review.

This is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) and healthy controls (n=33), uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM), and reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls. Methods report MNI-based preprocessing and whole-brain VBM with FWE correction; results describe whole-brain atrophy maps and comparisons of bvFTD groups versus NC. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes a bvFTD group, n=13), and I5 (bvFTD group ≥6; control group n=20 ≥6). However it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), nor does it present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result coming from a bvFTD vs control contrast (I7 not met). The VBM analyses described are correlational across a combined patient cohort and significant effects are reported only within pre-specified regional volumes of interest (ROI) after whole-brain FWE correction yielded no significant clusters; thus the reported significant findings are effectively ROI-based. Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI results with no whole-brain results for the target contrast/group) applies. Full text appears complete.

This paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on T1 MRI (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=14) (I4) and healthy control participants (controls reported and used in imaging contrasts; sample sizes exceed 6) (I5). The study reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and voxelwise regression analyses performed in SPM/ANTs mapped to a canonical stereotactic (MNI) space with peak voxels and cluster results summarized (I6, I7). Reporting of whole-brain results is explicit in text/tables/figures (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, reviews, seed-only FC, DTI, or cortical thickness only) apply. Therefore, the study should be INCLUDED.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and presents group-level, voxelwise comparisons of FTD subtypes vs healthy controls, including a bvFTD vs control contrast with MNI-coordinate reporting and brain maps (I6, I7, I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=49) and healthy controls (n=27), both exceeding the minimum N=6 (I4, I5). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical original research (not a review), reports whole-brain VBM results (not ROI-only), does not rely solely on excluded modalities, and excludes comorbid diagnoses per participant screening. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) sample (51 bv-FTD patients) (I4); has sufficient sample sizes (51 patients, 14 healthy controls) (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls using SPM5 with whole-brain correction thresholds (FWE/FDR) and cluster reporting (I6); provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported in text/figures and supplemental tables (e.g., table e-1) (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an original empirical VBM study (not a review), not ROI-only, does not use excluded modalities only, and does not indicate disqualifying comorbid sample characteristics. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons with MNI coordinates for a frontal-variant FTD (FTD-fv) group versus controls. FTD-fv corresponds to the behavioral/ frontal variant of FTD (bvFTD) targeted by the review. Sample sizes meet the minimum (25 FTD-fv patients; 14 controls). The paper reports group-level whole-brain results (FWE-corrected and uncorrected thresholds) and provides coordinates for significant clusters (e.g., left ITG/MTG at MNI −36, −4, −46 and right orbital gyrus at 10, 54, −18). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and is appropriate for inclusion in the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

Exclusion criterion E7 met: the study sample includes patients with coexisting motor neuron disease (MND) (13 of 58 candidates; 5/15 in CDR 0.5, 5/15 in CDR 1, 3/15 in CDR 2-3), which represents concurrent neurological disease and therefore violates the requirement for no other neurological symptoms. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients per group and >=6 controls), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level results, whole-brain corrected), and I8 (coordinates/figures described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all required inclusion criteria I3–I8 satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Although the authors reanalyzed data excluding patients with MND and found largely unchanged results, the original sample includes participants with neurological comorbidity, so the study must be excluded under E7.

The study reports empirical VBM (voxel-based morphometry) structural MRI analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=20) and healthy controls (n=39). Whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons versus controls are described (MNI space), and neuroimaging results (including reward-network–masked and follow-up whole-brain analyses with coordinates/clusters) are reported. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD and controls >6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (bvFTD n=10) and uses relevant imaging modalities (task fMRI and voxel-based morphometry), and has adequate group sizes for patients and controls (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, the voxelwise structural MRI analyses combined bvFTD and PNFA into a single group for whole-brain contrasts; the paper does not report a separate whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrast of bvFTD alone versus controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore criteria I6 and I7 (an unpooled bvFTD vs control voxelwise result) are not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This Neuron study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=72) and healthy controls, uses voxelwise structural MRI analyses (VBM-style W-score maps) and resting-state fMRI connectivity, and reports group- and region-level whole-brain voxelwise results in standard space (MNI) used to identify epicenters and atrophy patterns. Sample sizes exceed minimums and bvFTD results are analyzed separately from svPPA. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain results, not ROI-only, includes VBM/fMRI). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and STAR Methods; supplemental material referenced. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

Excluded because the study used structural ROI volumetric MRI analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3) and did not report any whole-brain voxelwise/coordinate-based between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). This makes it an ROI-only study, invoking exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD with a frontal variant group consistent with bvFTD) and I5 (patient and control group sizes exceed 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modalities), I6 (no between-group contrasts in defined stochastic space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses VBM and FDG-PET (meets I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the pooled FTLD group. However, it does not provide data specific to behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) with sufficient sample size: only 4 FTD patients are listed (FTD n=4, SD n=5, mixed n=2), so the bvFTD subgroup (if FTD corresponds to bvFTD) has fewer than 6 participants, violating I4/I5. The FTLD subtypes are pooled for group analyses, so there is no between-group contrast in standard stereotactic space that isolates a bvFTD group vs. controls (violates I6 and I7). Controls (n=13) meet the control size requirement, but the target clinical sample criterion is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis targeting bvFTD-specific whole-brain results.

This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) (I4) with an 8-subject control group (I5). VBM analyses were performed in Talairach space with voxelwise, group-level comparisons by diagnostic group, and the paper reports between-group VBM results (bvFTD vs controls) with cluster locations and coordinates (I6, I7). Whole-brain voxelwise results for bvFTD minus controls (lateral orbitofrontal gyrus, BA10) are reported; results and coordinates are presented in tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study meets all imaging and sample criteria for inclusion. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (bvFTD C9+ and bvFTD noncarriers vs controls) with familywise-error–corrected results and MNI coordinates (figures/tables). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (C9+ bvFTD n=15; bvFTD noncarriers n=48) and healthy controls (recruited, >6), satisfying minimum group sizes. Results include group-level whole-brain contrasts specific to the bvFTD group (not pooled with other syndromes), reported in text, figures, and tables. Full article contains methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of voxelwise findings. Therefore the paper satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a bvFTD VBM meta-analysis. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). The patient sample includes 8 clinically diagnosed FTD cases (classified per Neary criteria, consistent with behavioral-variant FTD) and 12 SemD (I4). Sample sizes meet thresholds (8 FTD patients; 20 controls) (I5). The paper reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in standardized space (MNI, with localization to Talairach atlases) including FTD vs controls (FTD not pooled with other groups) (I6,I7). Results are reported in figures/tables and described in text (I8). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion so is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply based on the provided content.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the imaging modality used is F-Flortaucipir (tau) PET and structural MRI/cortical thickness, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. It does meet I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD C9orf72 mutation carriers), I5 (patient group n=6 and controls n=54), I6 (reports between-group voxel-wise contrasts comparing the bvFTD/C9orf72 group to controls in MNI space), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise, group-level results for the target bvFTD sample), and I8 (voxelwise results are clearly described/figured). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This autopsy-confirmed VBM study includes a clearly defined subgroup of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=15 tau-positive + n=30 TDP-43-positive) and age-/gender-matched controls (n=35). Whole-brain, voxelwise SPM/VBM analyses are reported (FWE/FDR-corrected results presented as surface renders and coronal slices) comparing bvFTD groups to controls and assessing disease-stage contrasts, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Imaging modality (VBM), sample size thresholds, presence of bvFTD subgroup, and between-group whole-brain contrasts are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (19 bvFTD patients) with an adequate sample size and controls, but it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Imaging results are reported as regression associations within the combined FTLD cohort and small-volume-corrected loci; authors explicitly state no VBM association for the bvFTD (fvFTLD) subgroup alone and direct contrasts between subgroups did not reveal relevant effects. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria requiring between-group voxelwise results for the target bvFTD sample and whole-brain group-level results coming from the target group.

The full text reports an empirical neuroimaging study of clinically diagnosed bv-FTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI and 18F-FDG PET with partial-volume correction. Sample sizes meet thresholds (15 bv-FTD, 15 controls). The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise between-group SPM analyses (MRI and PET) with thresholding and reports results in tables/figures (coordinates implied via tables/figures and use of MNI template for normalization). It also conducts voxelwise intermodality correlations and direct voxelwise comparisons, all at the group level. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because key inclusion criteria are not met: I3 (modality) — the study uses F-THK5351 tau PET (and FLUTE amyloid PET), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; I5 (sample size) — bvFTD patient group has n=3 (<6 required); I6 (stereotactic coordinate reporting) — although voxel-wise SPM analyses are reported as figures/regions, the full text does not provide results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients included), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) and healthy controls (n=11). It reports between-group contrasts (controls vs bvFTD) in MNI-normalized space with voxelwise, whole-brain results (FWE whole-brain and small-volume corrected findings) for multiple contrasts. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; includes whole-brain results; not limited to ROI-only or non-fMRI modalities; no evidence of disqualifying comorbid sample).

The study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it used FDG-PET (I3); enrolled clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD patients consistent with behavioral variant FTD/Neary criteria (I4); included 22 patients and 15 controls (I5); reports voxelwise SPM group contrasts with peak coordinates given in Talairach space comparing the FTD group to controls (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly attributed to the target FTD sample (I7); and reports coordinates and results in text/tables (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met. Hence INCLUDE.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the required clinical-sample specificity (I4) and does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates for between-group contrasts (I6) based on the provided full text. Details: (a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM/TBM imaging methods — UVTBM builds on VBM/TBM), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: FTD N=30, controls N=14), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM comparisons for FTD vs controls). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not specify that the FTD sample is behavioral variant FTD or Pick’s disease — paper only states “FTD”), I6 (the provided text describes voxelwise SPMs and figures but does not provide coordinates in MNI or Talairach space or explicit coordinate tables for the FTD vs control contrast). Therefore the study cannot be included for a meta-analysis specifically targeting bvFTD coordinate-based whole-brain results.

This study uses VBM (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI space (I6, I7, I8) with adequate sample sizes (18 patients, 15 controls) meeting the sample-size criterion (I5). However, the patient group is ALS-FTD (frontotemporal dementia comorbid with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), not explicitly clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Pick’s disease; moreover, participants have concurrent neurological disease (ALS), which violates exclusion criterion E7 (samples with other neurological symptoms). Therefore I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s disease diagnosis) is not met and E7 applies, so the study must be excluded.

Full text is complete and study meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses resting FDG-PET), I4 (includes frontal variant FTD, which corresponds to behavioral variant FTD per Neary criteria), I5 (patient groups: fv-FTD n=18; controls n=18), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM correlations within the fv-FTD group), and I8 (results reported in tables/figures). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing the fv-FTD (bvFTD) group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (the reported SPM analyses are within-group correlations of fluency scores with FDG uptake rather than patient-versus-control voxelwise contrasts). Because I6 is required and is not satisfied, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met.

This study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise results specifically for the bvFTD subgroup. The paper uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the sample (7 bvFTD cases, meets I4), and sample sizes meet the minimum (meets I5). However, the authors combined bvFTD and avPPA GRN+ patients for the group-level analyses and explicitly state the small sample size prevented subanalysis by clinical phenotype; no between-group contrast is reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and no whole-brain result is clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, whole-brain analyses were performed for the combined patient group). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM contrasts (FDR-corrected) comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls with MNI coordinates provided (Table 2 and figures). Sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD N=26; controls N=16; imaging subset bvFTD N=21, controls N=12). Results include between-group contrasts in MNI space and whole-brain VBM analyses clearly identified for the target bvFTD sample. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all imaging, sample size, and reporting requirements for inclusion.

This study used VBM (and TBM) and included 37 FTD patients (satisfying I3 and sample size I5). However, it did not specifically recruit or report results for a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup: the authors analyzed FTD as a single pooled group (they note multiple clinical syndromes and only a few explicitly labelled bvFTD cases). Therefore I4 (bvFTD-specific sample) is not met. The paper does not present between-group contrasts that isolate a bvFTD-only group versus controls in a defined stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) — the reported voxelwise/ROI results are for pooled FTD, so I6 is not met. Although voxelwise VBM/TBM were performed, the whole-brain results apply to the mixed FTD group rather than a bvFTD target sample, so I7 is not met. Consequently the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) cohort (n=10) and controls (n=10). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts between each disease cohort (including bvFTD) and controls are reported (thresholds and spaces described; SPM outputs in MNI space and DARTEL outputs considered), satisfying requirements for between-group voxelwise results. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 threshold. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-empirical, inappropriate modality) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities or report whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only regional/lobar volumetric analyses with no whole-brain/voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD per Neary criteria, which corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD) and I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=12, controls n=24). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — used volumetric segmentation of structural MRI), I6 (no between-group results reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates for a bvFTD group), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the modality and whole-brain/coordinate-based requirements for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses FDG-PET and VBM), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients — 8 symptomatic carriers), I5 (patient group and control group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report a whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrast specifically comparing the bvFTD (symptomatic) group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Voxelwise analyses reported in the paper are for MAPT mutation carriers (symptomatic + asymptomatic) versus non-carriers; the authors explicitly state the three diagnostic groups were too small to do voxel-based imaging analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Because the key requirement of a voxelwise whole-brain contrast specifically for the bvFTD group versus controls is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) (I4) and an age-matched control group (n=23) meeting the minimum sample size requirement (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group VBM comparisons of each patient group versus controls, including bvFTD versus controls (I6, I7), and results are reported in MNI standard space with referenced atlases and cluster-level statistics; supplementary materials are available (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain results (E5,E6,E8,E9 not applicable), and participants with concurrent psychiatric/neurological comorbidities or substance abuse were explicitly excluded (so E7 not met). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore, INCLUDE for the review.

This is a whole-brain VBM study of genetic FTD mutation carriers vs noncarriers, reporting voxelwise group-level results. However, the study does not present a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group distinct from other FTD phenotypes; contrasts are between genetic carrier groups and noncarriers rather than a bvFTD clinical group versus controls. Therefore it does not meet the key inclusion requirements for (I4) clinical bvFTD sample and (I6) between-group contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM imaging), I5 (sample sizes: patient and control groups >=6), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) and healthy controls (n=34), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses comparing patient groups to controls (results and images referenced in supplementary material). Patient-control VBM comparisons were performed and significance thresholds and correction methods (FWE, TFCE, permutation testing) are specified; bvFTD vs. controls comparisons are described, and the VBM results are stated to replicate visual-rating findings. The full text provides Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary VBM figures/tables are referenced as online material (missing supplements are acceptable per instructions). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no prohibited modality-only study, and no indication of disqualifying comorbid sample). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of bvFTD whole-brain VBM studies.

This resting-state fMRI study evaluates dynamic whole-brain connectivity (chronnectome) in 128 FTD patients, including 81 bvFTD patients, and reports correlations between education and metastate metrics. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD subgroup n=81 >6). However, the paper lacks a healthy control group and does not report any between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). It reports within-patient correlational metrics and group-level metastate indices rather than voxelwise whole-brain group comparisons or coordinate tables. Therefore I6 and I7 are not satisfied, and the study does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise between-group results. Full text appears complete. Exclusion criteria: none explicitly met.

This article reports an empirical VBM study in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (23 patients after exclusions) with a healthy control group (n=20). Imaging modality: whole-brain voxelwise VBM (with group two-sample t-test and voxelwise regression analyses) was used and results are reported at the group level (whole-brain voxelwise comparisons and clusters reported). Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6 per group). The between-group two-sample t-test comparing bvFTD to controls and whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses are clearly described and reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, unsupported imaging modality) are triggered. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and contains the required whole-brain coordinate-based/voxelwise results.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement to include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease patients specifically. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET as an imaging modality) and I5 (patient group: 14 FTLD patients; control group: 13 controls — both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (patients are described as FTLD without specification that they are behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 and I7 (the paper does not report whole-brain, between-group voxelwise results specifically for a bvFTD group in MNI/Talairach space — results concern heterogeneous FTLD vs AD vs controls and ROI coordinates were taken from prior meta-analyses rather than reporting bvFTD-specific voxelwise contrasts). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses FDG-PET (I3) in a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD sample (fv-FTD, equivalent to bvFTD for purposes of sample; I4) with n=13 patients and control groups >6 (I5). It reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM correlations between resting FDG uptake and autobiographical memory measures within the patient group (group-level whole-brain results from the target sample; I7) and presents results in figures/tables/coordinates (I8). However, the paper does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrast (patient vs. control) in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD (fv-FTD) to controls (I6 not met). The meta-analysis requires at least one between-group whole-brain contrast; absence of such contrasts means the study does not meet all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered.

This study does not meet the key inclusion criterion I6: it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups). The paper reports resting-state fMRI whole-brain voxelwise correlations between Reserve Index and network connectivity within FTD patients and within presymptomatic GRN carriers, including MNI coordinates (satisfying I7 and I8). It also meets I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases, n=18), and I5 (patient groups exceed 6 participants). However, because there is no patient-vs-control whole-brain between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls (and no conventional healthy control group comparison reported), I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. The paper uses whole-brain voxelwise structural MRI analyses consistent with VBM-like methods (I3 met). However, it does not report results from a clinically defined behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick disease group contrasted with controls (I4 not met; clinical sample is a mixed FTD-spectrum/autopsy-defined grouping rather than explicitly bvFTD). The MRI subgroup that produced voxelwise maps is small (tau-positive n=5; tau-negative n=4; AD n=3), so the patient-group size requirement (≥6) for imaging contrasts is not satisfied (I5 not met). The paper does present voxelwise whole-brain atrophy maps for pathologically defined subgroups, but it does not present a between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a volumetric structural MRI study using region-based segmentation of the basal forebrain rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET and does not report voxelwise/MNI or Talairach coordinates. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (reports ROI/volume analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient and control groups each >6). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is T1 structural volumetry, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space for bvFTD), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on voxelwise VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET whole-brain results comparing bvFTD to controls.

This is an empirical longitudinal volumetric MRI study using semi-automated whole brain and ventricular boundary shift integrals (BBSI/VBSI), not VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants) and I5 (bvFTD group n=11; control group n=24). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space for bvFTD), I7 (no group-level whole‑brain voxelwise results in defined stochastic space), and I8 (no coordinate tables/voxelwise figures for such contrasts). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the imaging and voxelwise reporting requirements and must be excluded.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (sample size ≥6 in patient group), I8 (reports whole-brain results in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (study sample comprises genetic FTD mutation carriers but does not clearly report a clinically diagnosed bvFTD-only patient group or breakdown by bvFTD diagnosis), I6 (no between-group contrast directly comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a clinically diagnosed bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

Excluded because the study does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise group-level results for a clearly defined bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) sample. The paper includes 30 “FTD” patients but does not specify behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). Although VBM in MNI space was used (I3 met) and patient group sizes exceed 6 (I5 met), the reported results are ROI-based volumes/ROC analyses derived from z-score maps rather than reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts with coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). This means the paper effectively reports ROI/summary-based results rather than voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps, meeting exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results). Therefore it must be excluded.

This full-text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses alongside diffusion MRI, includes a clearly defined clinical bvFTD group (13 bvFTD patients diagnosed by established criteria) and matched healthy controls, and presents group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) VBM/TBSS results in MNI space comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=13; controls n=25). Whole-brain VBM results are described and overlaid on the MNI template; methods detail normalization to MNI space. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study includes FDG-PET and reports on FTD patients (n=36) but does not provide clear whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) to healthy controls in the main text. While voxel-based SPM was used for FDG analyses and supplemental tables/maps are referenced, the provided full text does not present group-level coordinate results or explicit bvFTD-versus-controls contrasts required by the review (I6, I7). Therefore, although imaging modality (FDG-PET) and adequate FTD sample size are met, the necessary whole-brain voxelwise coordinate evidence specific to bvFTD is not demonstrably reported in the accessible text, so the study does not satisfy all inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical MRI study that meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) alongside DTI, performs voxel-wise whole-brain SPM analyses in MNI space comparing bvFTD patients to controls (I6, I7), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (13 bvFTD cases) within the sample (I4), and both the patient subgroup and the control group exceed the minimum size of 6 participants (I5). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD versus control contrast are reported and clearly identified (I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. It uses conventional structural MRI measurements (manual distance/atrophy ratios and a novel FA index) rather than VBM, FDG-PET, or fMRI (I3 not met). The sample is described as clinically diagnosed FTD but the paper does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease explicitly (I4 not met). The study compares FTD to an Alzheimer’s disease patient group, not to healthy controls, and does not report between-group contrasts of bvFTD versus controls in standard stereotaxic space (I6 not met). No whole-brain voxelwise (e.g., VBM) group-level results in MNI/Talairach coordinates are reported (I7/I8 not met). The paper reports only regional/ROI-style measures (distance ratios/frontal atrophy) and no whole-brain voxelwise results, which meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (patient group N≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I6, I7, I8. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=33) and age-matched healthy controls, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts normalized to MNI space. Methods specify VBM preprocessing, two-sample t-tests comparing each disease group (including bvFTD) to controls, with results displayed as statistical maps and supplementary tables. The study thus meets imaging modality (VBM), sample (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), sample size (>6 per group), reporting of between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space, and whole-brain group-level results (figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed comorbid samples, not non-empirical, and not limited to DTI/seed-only FC). Full text is present (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study includes bvFTD patients and reports whole-brain VBM results, but it does not present a voxelwise between-group contrast directly comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. It reports VBM comparisons between AD and bvFTD (and behavioral comparisons with controls), but the imaging between-group contrasts required by the review (bvFTD vs healthy controls) are not provided. Therefore not all inclusion criteria are met.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3 met), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (I4 met), and has adequate group sizes (C9ORF72 group n=11; controls n=15) (I5 met). However, the between-group voxelwise contrasts reported are for a genetic subgroup (C9ORF72 mutation carriers) that pools multiple clinical syndromes (bvFTD, FTD–MND, PPA, etc.), not for a bvFTD-only patient group. Therefore the study does not provide a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in standard space (I6 not met) and does not clearly report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributable specifically to a bvFTD-only target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Conclusion: Excluded because it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (results are for a mixed-diagnosis genetic subgroup rather than a bvFTD-only group).

This retrospective case series uses 18F-FDG PET (meets I3) and reports a group of frontotemporal dementia patients (n=7) diagnosed with bvFTD criteria (meets I4) with at least 6 patients in the FTD group (meets I5). However, the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), nor does it provide whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures required for meta-analysis. There is no healthy control imaging group or BVFTD-vs-control statistical maps/coordinates (fails I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria from the review list (E5–E9) are directly met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This FDG-PET study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including mentions of behavioural-variant FTD) and uses FDG-PET (I3, I4). The FTD patient group is large enough to satisfy sample-size requirements (I5). However, the paper reports only expert visual readings and diagnostic concordance/sensitivity/specificity; it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Excluded on the basis of absence of voxelwise whole-brain results needed for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) with an adequate bvFTD subgroup size (I4, I5) and has full text available, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast that is specific to the bvFTD subgroup versus healthy controls. The study reports SPM comparisons for an aggregated FTD group (mixed FTD spectrum) versus controls and FDG-PET results linked to presence of primitive reflexes across the whole sample, but no bvFTD-only voxelwise results (thus failing I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results as required.

This is an empirical voxel-wise structural MRI study (longitudinal Jacobian/gray-matter change maps), equivalent to VBM-style analyses, that specifically includes a bvFTD group (n=44) and healthy controls (n=97). Analyses were performed in standardized (MNI) space and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing each FTLD variant (including bvFTD) to controls, with resulting consensus ROI/change maps and effect-size estimates. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study uses VBM (satisfies I3) and has patient groups with n>6 (satisfies I5). However, it does not include participants who were clinically diagnosed with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). There are no reported between-group contrasts comparing a clinically-defined bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons (FTLD-U vs controls; FTLD-MND vs controls) with MNI-based normalization and voxelwise thresholds. Patient group sizes meet the minimum (FTLD-U n=11; FTLD-MND n=7) and the control group (n=18) meets the criterion. All cases fulfilled consensus criteria for frontotemporal dementia and the paper refers to a clinical diagnosis of frontal-variant/frontotemporal dementia, consistent with behavioral-variant FTD for the purposes of this review. The paper provides group-level whole-brain VBM results in text/figures and identifies affected regions. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; modality is VBM). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. Note: the only minor uncertainty is that the manuscript does not repeatedly label subjects explicitly as “bvFTD” in every section, but it states they fulfilled consensus criteria for frontotemporal dementia and discusses frontal-variant cases, so inclusion is justified.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used whole-brain Voxel-Based Morphometry (I3) with images normalized to MNI space; included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4) and healthy controls (n=21) (I5); reports voxelwise whole-brain VBM results and correlations (FWE-corrected, MNI-normalized) and performs group comparisons/post-hoc tests including bvFTD vs controls (I6, I7). Whole-brain results and supplementary data are referenced and qualifying results appear reported in text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed FTD patients with behavioral-variant cases present (I4) and sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=24; I5). However, the analyses are graph-theory based on a 471-region parcellation and report regional/parcel-wise network metrics rather than voxelwise, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts. Therefore it does not provide the required between-group, voxelwise whole-brain results (I6 and I7 not met). Because no voxelwise whole-brain coordinate results are reported and analyses are region/parcellation-based only, exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/parcellation analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results) applies. Full text appears complete. Exclusion rationale: fails I6 and I7; meets I3,I4,I5; exclusion E6 applies.

This is a protocol/methods paper describing the LEFFTDS cohort and procedures; it does not present empirical, between-group whole-brain imaging results comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease patients to controls. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical/methods-only paper). Inclusion criteria: I3 (uses fMRI acquisition) is satisfied in that the protocol includes intrinsic connectivity (resting-state) fMRI acquisition. The study includes FDG-PET imaging and clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with sufficient sample sizes (I3, I4, I5 are satisfied). The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses of cerebellar subregions from T1-weighted MRI (atlas-based label fusion), with no voxelwise whole-brain (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET results and no stereotactic coordinates. EXCLUSION: E6 (study reports ROI-based/region-based structural MRI analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Imaging and sample meet some inclusion criteria: the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=15) (I4) with at least 6 patients and controls present (I5). (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 - study reports only ROI (manual segmentation of hippocampus and amygdala) with no whole-brain voxelwise results. The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and outcome reporting criteria required by the review. This study uses structural MRI (voxelwise W-score maps/voxel-based morphometry procedures) and has adequate group sizes, but it does NOT meet key review inclusion requirements. Specifically, the sample is familial FTLD mutation carriers pooled across MAPT/GRN/C9orf72 and heterogeneous clinical diagnoses — the paper does not present results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) or Pick’s disease group (I4 not met). The reported analyses summarize voxelwise W-scores within 179 atlas ROIs and use a machine-learning classifier and ROI-integrated weights rather than reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) statistical contrasts with coordinate tables; thus there are no qualifying between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM-type structural MRI methods) and I5 (sample sizes >6). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI/summary-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Therefore the study is excluded for not containing bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise between-group coordinates or a dedicated bvFTD patient group.

The study uses FDG-PET (meets I3) but does not explicitly report inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease patients (I4 not met). The manuscript reports inclusion of ‘FTLD’ patients but does not specify bvFTD subtype or provide subgroup counts for bvFTD, so it is not possible to confirm the required patient group. The paper does not present any between-group voxel-wise contrasts with coordinates in MNI or Talairach space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met). Also, the bvFTD/FTLD subgroup sample size is not clearly reported for the whole-brain analyses to verify the ≥6 participants requirement (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with bvFTD among the phenotypes (I4), and has adequate group sizes (30 FTD, 35 controls; I5). However, it does not present a between-group, voxelwise contrast that isolates a bvFTD group compared directly to healthy controls (I6). The reported voxelwise FDG-PET result is a correlation of metabolism with prosocial sexual behavior across a combined patient sample (FTD and CBS), not a whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise result derived from a bvFTD-only vs control contrast (I7). Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 and cannot be included in the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study that reports group-level voxelwise comparisons for a bvFTD sample. The paper uses VBM (satisfies I3) and includes an ALS-FTD subgroup meeting bvFTD criteria (authors state all ALS-FTD met bvFTD criteria) (satisfies I4). The bvFTD/ALS-FTD group size is 7 and controls n=24, meeting the >=6 participants requirement (I5). The manuscript reports between-group contrasts comparing ALS-FTD (bvFTD) to controls with voxelwise VBM results (significant caudate head cluster, FWE-corrected) and refers to Supplementary Table 2 (implying coordinate reporting), satisfying I6 and I7. Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a fronto-temporal dementia (FTD) patient group of n=13 (I5). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of FTD versus controls in Talairach space (I6, I7) and presents results in acceptable forms (I8). However, the paper does not specify that the FTD sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease; diagnostic subtype is not detailed, so inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD or Pick's disease) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (specific diagnosis of bvFTD/Pick's).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=20) and age-matched healthy controls (n=20). Whole-brain voxel-wise VBM analyses (permutation-based GLM) comparing patient groups to controls are reported, with results localised using the Harvard-Oxford atlas and maximum coordinates reported in MNI space. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD group (including atrophy patterns and correlations with behavioural measures), satisfying the requirement for between-group contrasts specific to bvFTD. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not DTI/FC/cortical-thickness-only; empirical data only). The provided full text contains introduction, methods (including VBM procedures), results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This study uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (satisfies I3) and the sample includes some clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (satisfies I4). However, it is excluded because it does not report any between-group contrasts specifically comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met), and it does not present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for a bvFTD-only sample (I7 not met). Additionally, the number of clinically defined bvFTD participants is not reported separately, so the requirement for at least 6 bvFTD patients in the target group cannot be confirmed (I5 not met). The paper analyzes pathologically defined FTLD-TDP subtypes rather than a clinician-diagnosed bvFTD group, so the target sample results required by the review objective are absent. Exclusion criteria: none met.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; N=74) and I5 (patient group >=6). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (study does not use Voxel-Based Morphometry, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET — it uses visual rating of conventional structural MRI), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in standard (MNI/Talairach) space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy required imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria and must be excluded from the review.

Meets all inclusion criteria: uses FDG-PET voxelwise analysis (SPM) (I3); participants are clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTLD (fv-FTLD), equivalent to bvFTD in intent (I4); sample sizes meet thresholds (18 patients, 24 controls; MDL subset 8 and 6) (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space comparing fv-FTLD to controls (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the target fv-FTLD sample (I7); results reported as coordinates and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study uses VBM-like voxel-wise GM/CSF analyses (I3), includes FTD patients with bvFTD among them (I4), and has adequate group sizes (30 FTD, 30 controls; I5), it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast in standard stereotactic space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other FTD subtypes. The FTD sample is a mixed group (bvFTD and semantic dementia) and the paper presents individual deviation maps, region-wise ROC/classification results and reader-based comparisons rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts or coordinate tables for a bvFTD vs control comparison. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Full text appears complete.

The study uses VBM-based processing of structural MRI (I3 satisfied) and includes a test FTD group (n=12) and healthy controls (n=18), meeting sample-size requirements (I5 satisfied). However, it does NOT specify that the FTD cases are clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; FTD is reported without subtyping, so I4 is not met. Crucially, the paper does not report any whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast coordinates in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls; results are presented as classifier performance (SVM AUCs, PPV/NPV) and radar plots rather than voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables, so I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not include a healthy/control group nor report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met). It is an open-label before/after FDG-PET study with within-subject and subgroup (bvFTD n=7) voxelwise contrasts, but no case–control comparison. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included), I5 (patient group and bvFTD subgroup ≥6 participants), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for bvFTD subgroup), I8 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires between-group voxelwise contrasts vs controls where bvFTD is not pooled, this paper does not meet I6 and must be excluded.

Although the study used FDG-PET (meets I3) and included an FTD patient group larger than 6 (meets I5), it does not meet key review requirements: the paper does not specify that patients had behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease (I4 not satisfied), and it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (in MNI/Talairach space) comparing a bvFTD group to controls — no coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps are provided (I6 and I7 not satisfied). Imaging analyses were visual reads and PALZ classifications rather than voxelwise group comparisons. Therefore it must be excluded under E6 (no whole-brain results reported).

This paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing MSTD mutation carriers (early-stage bvFTD cases) to age- and gender-matched controls. Methods explicitly describe optimized and modulated VBM (SPM2) and report statistically significant voxelwise grey matter loss (P<0.05 FDR-corrected) with stereotactic locations referenced in supplementary Table 4. The sample used for VBM comprised 7 MSTD patients (bvFTD; early-stage) and 19 controls, satisfying minimum group sizes. The results are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and coordinate/stereotactic localization is provided (in supplemental). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, contains whole-brain voxelwise results, not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; supplementary coordinate table is referenced. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8).

The study uses VBM and includes a bvFTD subgroup (I3, I4) with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=11; controls n=39) (I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are correlations within the combined FTLD patient cohort and results are reported using pre-specified small-volume (ROI) correction; the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group separately to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (a between-group contrast for bvFTD vs controls and at least one whole-brain group-level voxelwise result from the bvFTD group) are not met. In addition, the reported significant imaging finding derives from ROI/small-volume analysis rather than whole-brain voxelwise results, fitting exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets inclusion criteria for the review via its Pick disease (PiD) subgroup.
